milestone: M49 Headless Mode Pack Update Drive

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets public headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive carry a registry-selection target into Rust-owned run-control instead of requiring caller-owned continue_once glue.
Bootstraps the Mode Pack update route chain from registry selection into selected-candidate fetch using existing typed continuation authority.
Requires explicit target authorization, route-boundary validation, bounded one-step execution, and matching replay identity before side effects.
Preserves run-session evidence and fails closed when subordinate route evidence is absent or mismatched during replay.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive can route a bounded registry update selection target through public run-control and can reject corrupted routed replay when subordinate fetch evidence is missing.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: headless.continue_once can perform registry selection and M49.1 can fetch from an already-persisted route, but public run-control could not bootstrap the registry-selection-to-fetch boundary under session authority.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still own out-of-band route sequencing and replay could accept a persisted selected-candidate fetch route without the underlying fetch checkpoint.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M47.1 rolled back active replacement, M48.1 selected a registry update through continue_once, and M49.1 fetched an already-routed selected candidate; M49.2 bootstraps the public route chain and hardens replay evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive are extended with a bounded target field and delegate to existing continuation authority.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It reuses bounded run-control and continuation evidence rather than adding reports, histories, digests, verdicts, inspections, or readiness summaries.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates explicit Mode Pack run-control targets, forwards registry selection through typed continuation authority, preserves session checkpoints, and fails closed when subordinate routed evidence is missing.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can keep the Mode Pack update route chain inside durable Rust-owned run-control from the first registry-selection step.
answers.milestone_progress: M49 moves from one pre-existing fetch-route bridge toward a real public Mode Pack update drive with replay-safe route evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M49.2 updates the current and archived value manifests for the route-bootstrap integrity phase.

exit_criteria: headless.run.advance can carry a bounded modepack_registry_update_selection_target through public run-control into a persisted fetch route
headless.run.drive can pass the same bounded target through its first runtime-owned advance
routed selected-candidate fetch replay fails closed when subordinate fetch checkpoint evidence is missing
runtime rejects stale progress, wrong route, missing target, and request identity mismatch before side effects
VSIX protocol validators accept the bounded registry-selection run-control target and reject raw/unknown fields
behavior_evidence: Rust compile checks cover protocol/runtime request plumbing
Rust replay-integrity tests cover routed selected-candidate fetch missing evidence, missing target, and request identity mismatch
VSIX protocol tests validate run-control params with registry-selection target and raw field rejection
